payload.text: **THE LAYOUT IS A FLAT SCROLLING COLUMN OF `{title, value, type}` ROWS WITH NO DECORATION, AND THE ONLY FORMATTING GUARANTEE IS COLUMN ALIGNMENT.** Field names align in one column and values align in another, across the whole form -- **that alignment IS the design, so it is asserted rather than eyeballed**: every rendered row has its name starting at one column and its value at another, measured over a form whose longest name and longest value both exceed the viewport. **THE CHROME IS THE RATIFIED DESIGN'S, NOT THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL WORDING, AND IT HAS NOW BEEN CORRECTED TWICE.** This row said *one modeline at the foot above a single rule*; it was corrected on 2026-08-30 (vc, on ic's finding) to `tui-design.md` as ratified 2026-08-29 -- FIVE sections separated by TWO rules, APP ROW, BODY, then STATUS, COMMAND and INFO -- because a criterion that contradicts a ratified design is the criterion being stale rather than the design being wrong. **THAT CORRECTION LANDED ON A DESIGN THAT HAD ALREADY MOVED THE SAME DAY, WHICH IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART**: hv's omnibox ruling of 2026-08-30 collapsed the foot from three standing rows to two, so STATUS/COMMAND/INFO named a foot that no longer existed by the time the row was corrected to it. **THE AS-BUILT, MEASURED 2026-09-02: FOUR STANDING SECTIONS -- APP ROW, BODY, OMNIBOX ROW, HINT ROW -- separated by TWO rules, with a THIRD LABELLED rule appearing only when the body splits into list and detail.** The mode chip is the first thing on the HINT row rather than a section of its own. **AND THE BORDERS CLAUSE IS GONE FOR A DIFFERENT REASON: hv ratified the framed composer (O1, 2026-09-02), which is a border.** `no borders anywhere` was true when written and was overtaken by a ruling, so the guarantee this row makes is about DECORATION and ALIGNMENT, and the composer's frame is neither. **ic BUILT TO THIS ROW AND WAS RIGHT TO** -- they had read only section 3 and the row is what the register offered them, which is the whole hazard: a stale criterion is indistinguishable from a current one at the point of use. **THIRD INSTANCE OF THE DATED-MEASUREMENT CLASS ON THIS THREAD** after `AC-12.4` and `AC-17.6`, and the first where a row contradicts a ratified artefact rather than merely citing a moved surface -- so the class is not only about staleness in prose, it reaches rows that were never reconciled against a document written after them. **AND THE SECOND CORRECTION IS THE SHARPER LESSON: A ROW CORRECTED TO A DOCUMENT IS ONLY AS CURRENT AS THE READ THAT CORRECTED IT**, so a correction citing a ratification date needs the document re-read at the moment of writing, not the date trusted. **A field whose value does not fit is truncated visibly, never wrapped into a second row**, because a wrapped value breaks the one guarantee the layout makes.
